messages:
alex: noticing intermittent packet loss on geneve overlay in us-west-gpu cluster. training jobs see spikes in retransmits and occasional connection resets, mostly east-west between GPU nodes.
infra-bot: alert: cluster-us-west-gpu high tcp_retransmit_rate (threshold 2%). incident created -> INC-2026-307 @sre-oncall
maria: reported this morning too? any kernel/firmware bumps?
alex: we rolled a minor Mellanox FW update to ~10% of fleet last week. correlation but not 1:1. also saw MTU mismatch on a couple hosts — geneve mtus at 1500 while host nic expects 9000.
raj: can you paste `ip -d link show` for geneve and `ethtool -S` from an affected host? any RDMA counters?
alex: quick snippets from host-42 (affected):
```
root@host-42:~# ip -d link show geneve0
5: geneve0@NONE: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
    geneve id 100 remote 10.0.10.2 ttl 64 key 0x64 port 6081
root@host-42:~# ethtool -S ens2
NIC stats:
  rx_packets: 12451234
  rx_drop: 412
  tx_packets: 9871234
  tx_drop: 3
  rx_no_buffer: 7
```
Also saw `tcp_retransmits` in `ss -s` jump during the window.

maria: MTU mismatch will force fragmentation or host-side fallback. But geneve encaps adds ~42 bytes, so host MTU must be higher. Why are some geneve devices at 1500?

alex: kube CNI (calico) defaulted to 1500 on those nodes after a node pool reprovision. The rest stayed at 9000.

raj: that explains a lot. When a pod on jumbo hosts talks to pod on standard MTU host, encapsulated frame > host MTU -> drop or fragmentation depending on offloads. Check GSO/TSO/GRO offload stats too.

alex: ran `ethtool -k ens2` — GSO/TSO/GRO on by default. On affected host, after bumping traffic we see lots of `rx_drop` and some `gso_errors` in the kernel logs.

maria: short-term mitigations: 1) force host-side geneve MTU to 8950 on those nodes and restart CNI pods, OR 2) temporarily disable GSO for the tunnel interface (eg `ethtool -K geneve0 gso off gro off tso off`) while we fix reprovisioning. Both have perf/cpu tradeoffs.

raj: agree. For GPU training jobs we prefer less CPU overhead, so option 1 is better long-term. Can we automate a node-pool patch?

alex: will patch node-pool template to set `--mtu 8950` and roll non-critical nodes first. Doing a canary on 3 nodes now.

sre-oncall: FYI adding a temporary routing rule to prefer same-MTU nodes for scheduling until pool is fixed (k8s affinity). Also disabling RDMA RoCE on the two problematic hosts as a test — observed a handful of RoCE packet drops.

maria: disabling RoCE is a good probe. If RDMA path was tunneling it might expose MTU/segmentation edge cases. Keep an eye on QP reset counters.

alex: can confirm after forcing geneve0 mtu to 8950 on host-42, packet loss dropped to ~0.1% and training throughput normalized. Putting the kube node pool patch up as PR.

raj: follow-ups: 1) add node-provisioning check to ensure geneve MTU aligns with host MTU (preflight); 2) alert rule tweak to include `geneve0.mtu` divergence; 3) runbook entry for GSO/GRO toggle and perf impact.

maria: also add a post-deploy validation that Mellanox FW updates are rolled via canary and that RDMA counters are monitored.

alex: created PR #3428 for node-pool MTU fix, added runbook draft, and tagged infra-sre for validation.

infra-bot: deployment:node-pool-mtu-fix started by alex. logs -> https://ci.redwood/example/3428 

sre-oncall: marking incident INC-2026-307 as mitigated for now, leaving alerting at a higher sensitivity for 24h. :white_check_mark:

maria: nice triage folks. we'll keep monitoring and follow up on the runbook edits. :thumbsup:
